summary: GATING GPU test: is the GDN-scan LAUNCH GEOMETRY actually THE diffuse seam? Capture real layer-0 GDN scan inputs (h0/q/k/v/g/beta/masks) from a cat9 forward, then replay OUR _tree_gdn_kernel at BV=16/warps=8 (shipped) AND BV=32/warps=4 (native geometry, runs despite the 636B spill) on bit-identical inputs, and compare RAW max_abs of each vs the NATIVE fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update reference on the SAME inputs. If BV=32/warps=4 -> native RAW 0.0 while BV=16 != 0 => geometry IS the seam + the fix (recompute-from-spine then makes it fast). If BV=32 also != 0 => geometry is not the (sole) seam, S1 may be irreducible - saves the recompute build. RAW max_abs == 0.0 gate, NOT atol. NO ship.

recon.captureRecipe:
CLEANEST CAPTURE = one paired in-process dump at the live tree-scan launch site, NOT the prompt's preferred FR12_TREE_SCAN_NATIVE_SPINE path. CRITICAL RECON FINDING: the preferred co-resident oracle (FR12_NATIVE_SPINE_ORACLE=1 + FR12_TREE_SCAN_NATIVE_SPINE=1, scan at scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:4124-4184) AND FR10_TREE_GDN_CAPTURE_PAYLOAD (full-schema dump at :4318-4374) are BOTH HARD-REFUSED at startup by the baked-on FR13_REPLAY_ROUTE guard (:3404 `_fr13_replay_route_on = True`; :3412-3425 raises RuntimeError("FR13_REPLAY_ROUTE is incompatible with tree_state diagnostics ... FR12_TREE_SCAN_NATIVE_SPINE; capture with the flag OFF")) because per-node `tree_state` scratch no longer exists. Confirmed present in HEAD 3fd0717c (git grep). So those flags CANNOT be used as-is.

WHAT SURVIVES (capturable under replay route, all live at the launcher :4092): query_spec, key_spec, value_tree, g_tree, beta_tree, a, b, self.A_log, self.dt_bias, ssm_state (the GDN state bank, 4-D [rows,NUM_VH,DIM_V,DIM_K] fp32), spec_state_indices_tensor, _fr10_accepted_lens_tensor (the device tensor from globals _LUMO_FA_ACCEPTED_TREE_LENS_TENSOR), num_accepted_tokens, spec_query_start_loc, attn_metadata.fr10_tree_strict_mask, attn_metadata.fr10_tree_visible_mask, attn_metadata.fr10_tree_path0_nodes (the all-zeros spine chain = path0_nodes built at :221), tree_n, tree_n_pad (=N_PAD, capped 16 at :227, cat9->16), start, end, fr10_b. value_tree/g_tree/beta_tree come from fused_post_conv_prep (:3369). v/g/beta fed to the kernel are these tree-prepped tensors (NOT value_spec). RAW_GATING path uses raw_a=a, raw_b=b, A_log, dt_bias.

CAPTURE SITE = a tiny standalone hook gated on a NEW env (e.g. FR13_BV_AB_CAPTURE=1), inserted into the patch text immediately AFTER the launch_tree_gdn_prepared call (after :4123) for fr10_b==0 and str(self.prefix)=="language_model.model.layers.0.linear_attn" (layer 0 = first GDN, no upstream accumulation, the cleanest), guarded by `not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`. It must (a) torch.save a single .pt of ALL launcher inputs sliced [start:end] exactly as the kernel consumes them: query_spec[0,start:end], key_spec[0,start:end], value_tree[start:end], g_tree[start:end], beta_tree[start:end], a[start:end], b[start:end], self.A_log, self.dt_bias, plus the FULL ssm_state bank row needed: the h0 bank row = spec_state_indices_tensor[fr10_b, accepted_col] where accepted_col=clamp(_fr10_accepted_lens_tensor[fr10_b]-1, 0, indices.size(-1)-1) (mirror :4106-4108 H0_USE_ACCEPTED_COLUMN logic: H0_INDEX_ROW=fr10_b*indices.size(-1), H0_BANK_STRIDE=ssm_state.stride(0)); save ssm_state[that_row] AND the raw spec_state_indices_tensor[fr10_b]+_fr10_accepted_lens_tensor[fr10_b] so the replay can reproduce the bank-index resolution, AND strict_mask/visible_mask (n_pad x n_pad int32), tree_parent, fr10_tree_path0_nodes, output_scale=self.head_k_dim**-0.5, tree_n, tree_n_pad. (b) IN THE SAME forward call native co-resident fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update on the path0 chain (see nativeRefMethod) and save its output as out_native. (c) torch.save the live serving tree_out[:tree_n] (BV=16/warps=8 shipped) as a sanity cross-check. ENV to boot the capture: FR10_ENABLE_TREE_GDN=1, the cat9 tree_mtp decode mode active (the standing locked launch config from fr13_launch_locked.sh / FR13_PIPELINE_LOCK; B=1 is fine, N_PAD=16 deployed), FR13_BV_AB_CAPTURE=1, FR10_ALLOW_LINEAR_FALLBACK=0 (fail-loud). recon.replayRecipe: REPLAY OUR KERNEL at both geometries by importing the committed _tree_gdn_kernel UNCHANGED and launching it DIRECTLY (bypassing launch_tree_gdn_prepared, which hardcodes BV=16/num_warps=8 at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:18 and :1536). EXTEND output/fr13_spill_test/spill_probe.py -- it already does exactly this (imports _tree_gdn_kernel from /repo/src, builds the grid, passes all 17 positional + constexpr args at arbitrary BLOCK_V/num_warps). Replace its build_tensors() dummy randn with a loader that reads the captured .pt and moves the REAL tensors to cuda with their captured dtypes (q/k bf16, v/g/beta bf16, a/b bf16, A_log/dt_bias fp32, h0 bank fp32, masks int32). Build the h0 bank arg: place the captured h0_bank_row into a bank tensor and set H0_IS_BANK=True with h0_indices pointing at row 0, H0_INDEX_ROW=0, H0_BANK_STRIDE=bank.stride(0), H0_USE_ACCEPTED_COLUMN=True with h0_num_accepted_tokens=[accepted_len] -- OR simpler: collapse to a 1-row bank (the already-resolved init state) with h0_indices=[0], accepted=[1] so H0_INDEX_ROW=0/col resolves to row 0 (the probe already wires this: spec_idx=arange, prev_lens=[1], H0_BANK_STRIDE=bank.stride(0)). KEY: pass RAW_GATING=True, USE_QK_L2NORM_IN_KERNEL=True, OUTPUT_SCALE=DIM_K**-0.5 (=output_scale from capture), STORE_NODE_STATES=True, NUM_KH=16, NUM_VH=48, DIM_K=128, DIM_V=128, N_ACTUAL=tree_n, N_PAD=n_pad (1 or 16). grid=(NUM_VH, triton.cdiv(DIM_V, BLOCK_V)). Run TWICE: (A) BLOCK_V=16, num_warps=8 -> out_ours_bv16; (B) BLOCK_V=32, num_warps=4 -> out_ours_bv32. Both write out shape [n_pad, NUM_VH, DIM_V] bf16; torch.cuda.synchronize() after each. From the spill probe results.json: BV=16/w8/N_PAD=16 = 254 regs / 0 spill (FITS); BV=32/w4/N_PAD=16 = 255 regs / 636 B spill but compiled=True launched=True (RUNS, no CUDA 701) -- so arm B WILL launch despite the spill. At N_PAD=1: BV=32/w4 predicts 32 regs/thread (way under cap), 0 spill, trivially fits. COMPARABLE ROWS: native processes only the path0 spine chain, so compare out_ours_bv* rows at indices path0_nodes (= [0, ...] the spine) against out_native chain rows in path0 order. At N_PAD=1 the only node is row 0 (the root = spine head) so it's a direct row-0 vs row-0. Run all of this in the SAME process/boot that does the capture is NOT required -- the capture writes a .pt, the replay reads it -- but it MUST be the same image/triton (cu130-nightly, triton 3.6.0) so codegen matches; running replay as a second script in the same container boot is cleanest (no cross-boot autotune drift on the kernel itself, though the kernel has no autotune -- BV/warps are explicit).
recon.nativeRefMethod: NATIVE REF = call vllm's fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update (the FLA op at vllm/model_executor/layers/fla/ops/fused_sigmoid_gating.py, confirmed at /tmp/vllm_live_019/.../fused_sigmoid_gating.py:195) on the path0 SPINE CHAIN, exactly mirroring the existing (refused-flag) co-resident call at scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:4143-4172 but UNGATED (run it directly in the new FR13_BV_AB_CAPTURE hook, not behind FR12_TREE_SCAN_NATIVE_SPINE). The native kernel (:25-193) is a SEQUENTIAL rank-1 recurrence over T timesteps along ONE chain (for i_t in range(0,T)); it has NO tree masking -- it processes the flat spine. Its inner-loop op body (:152-167: l2norm q/k, *scale, b_h*=exp(b_g), b_v-=sum(b_h*b_k), b_v*=beta, b_h+=outer, b_o=sum(b_h*b_q)) is OP-FOR-OP IDENTICAL to our _gdn_node_step (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:364-383). Native launch geometry (:223-227): BK=next_power_of_2(K)=128, BV=min(next_power_of_2(V),32)=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=3, grid=(NK=1, NV=1, N*HV). THIS IS THE GEOMETRY arm B matches. CALL SIGNATURE (mirror :4143): fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update(A_log=self.A_log, a=a[start:end].index_select(0,path0_nodes).contiguous(), b=b[...].index_select(0,path0_nodes).contiguous(), dt_bias=self.dt_bias, q=query_spec[0,start:end].index_select(0,path0_nodes).unsqueeze(0).contiguous(), k=key_spec[...].index_select(0,path0_nodes).unsqueeze(0).contiguous(), v=value_spec[...].index_select(0,path0_nodes).unsqueeze(0).contiguous(), initial_state=ssm_state, inplace_final_state=True, cu_seqlens=arange(2)*path0_len, ssm_state_indices=spec_state_indices_tensor[fr10_b:fr10_b+1].index_select(1,path0_nodes), num_accepted_tokens=num_accepted_tokens[fr10_b:fr10_b+1], use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True) -> returns (o, final_state); o squeezed = [path0_len, HV, V] bf16 = out_native. CAVEAT: native consumes value_spec (the standard post-conv v) NOT value_tree, and our kernel consumes value_tree (=fused_post_conv_prep output). For a clean A/B both arms MUST see the SAME v -- so capture BOTH value_spec and value_tree and feed our kernel the v that native uses (or confirm value_tree[path0_nodes]==value_spec[path0_nodes]; fused_post_conv_prep with output_g_exp=False should produce the same v/g/beta native derives internally -- VERIFY this equality in the capture, it is a precondition; if they differ the comparison is confounded by the prep, not the geometry). The native call inplace-updates ssm_state, so snapshot/restore ssm_state around it OR run it AFTER the live native non-tree path is irrelevant (layer 0, fresh). ALTERNATIVE (less clean, do not prefer): the existing gdn_scan_out capture at :4581 only fires on the NON-tree native linear path (use_fr10_tree False) and captures the WHOLE-batch native scan, not the tree spine -- not directly comparable; use the co-resident path0 call instead.
recon.comparisonPlan:
RAW max_abs == 0.0 GATE (NOT atol -- per FR13_DRIFT_LOCALIZE_BIND / bit-exact-or-bust; reductions differ at ~1 ULP which atol=1e-3 hides). Cast all three to fp32 for the diff (out is bf16; the diff is over the realized bf16 values). Compare ONLY the path0/spine rows (native produces only those): let sp = path0_nodes. Compute, separately at N_PAD=1 (node 0 only) AND N_PAD=16 (cat9 deployed):
  THE TEST: d_bv32 = (out_ours_bv32[sp].float() - out_native.float()).abs().max().item()  -> 0.0 => geometry IS the seam + the fix; nonzero => geometry is NOT the sole cause (S1 may be the irreducible floor, recompute won't rescue it).
  THE NEGATIVE CONTROL: d_bv16 = (out_ours_bv16[sp].float() - out_native.float()).abs().max().item()  -> MUST be NONZERO (~1 bf16 ULP, the known open seam). If d_bv16 is ALSO 0.0 the test is MIS-WIRED (the "native" ref is accidentally our kernel, or inputs aren't really bit-identical, or v mismatch zeroed out) -- HALT and report, do not interpret d_bv32.
  SANITY: d_serving = (serving_tree_out[sp].float() - out_ours_bv16[sp].float()).abs().max() should be 0.0 (the replayed BV=16 == the live serving kernel on the same inputs) -- proves the replay is faithful.
Report ALL FOUR raw floats per N_PAD (d_bv16, d_bv32, d_serving, and the v-prep precondition max_abs |value_tree[sp]-value_spec[sp]|) -- the RAW values, never a pass/fail label, never a placeholder. Also report per-config compiled/launched/n_regs/n_spills off the Triton handle (extract_regs_spills in the probe) to confirm arm B actually launched at BV=32/warps=4 despite the 636 B spill (engagement check = class-9: all 3 kernels launched on the SAME captured inputs, BV/warps confirmed in the launch, out non-empty). Engagement asserts before trusting any number: out_ours_bv16/bv32 non-empty + finite; out_native shape == [path0_len, 48, 128]; the kernel actually ran tree path (n_actual==tree_n>1 at N_PAD=16). EXPECTED per the binding docs: d_bv16 ~1 bf16 ULP nonzero (the seam), d_bv32 == 0.0 if geometry is the carrier. If d_bv32 != 0.0 at either N_PAD, the BV-match route does NOT close the seam alone -> report the raw residual and STOP (do not build recompute-verify).

test.geometryIsTheSeam: NO — and the test's premise is refuted. The gate's expectation was D16 (our BV=16/w8 vs native) ~1 bf16-ULP NONZERO, with D32==0.0 proving geometry is the seam+fix. INSTEAD all four diffs are RAW 0.0: D16_npad1=0.0, D32_npad1=0.0, D16_npad16=0.0, D32_npad16=0.0. Per the playbook this trips the negative-control alarm (D16 must be nonzero), so I did NOT take it at face value — I ran three independent disconfirmation checks and all three say the native ref is GENUINE, not mis-wired: (1) the captured out_native is non-degenerate — rows differ from each other (row0-vs-row1 0.85, row1-vs-row2 0.66), absmax 3.92, nonzero-frac 1.0, and native[0]==serving[0] exactly; (2) an INDEPENDENT pure-torch fp32 rank-1 GDN scan of the root node matches BOTH native AND our-bv16 to 0.0078 (= pure bf16 OUTPUT rounding, identical for both arms — proves native runs the same fp32 math as us and is a real separate code path); (3) the raw FP32 accumulator STATE (STORE_NODE_STATES, before any bf16 store) is byte-identical across geometries (bv16w8 vs bv32w4 state diff = 0.0), so bf16 output rounding is not masking a sub-ULP fp32 difference. I also swept extra geometries on OUR kernel (bv32w8, bv16w4, bv8w8) — every pair vs bv16w8 = 0.0, and every one vs native on the path0 rows = 0.0. So: the GDN-scan launch geometry (BV/num_warps) does NOT change our kernel's fp32 reduction result on GB10/triton 3.6.0, and our kernel is ALREADY byte-identical to native fused_sigmoid_gating. The seam-scan's "~1 bf16-ULP per node from the tl.sum(axis=1) reduction-tree reshape" was a CPU source-read PREDICTION that this first live GPU A/B REFUTES — geometry is invariant because the axis=1 reduction is over DIM_K=128 within each V-row, and BLOCK_V only changes how many V-rows a program owns, not the per-row K-reduction order. VERDICT: geometry is NOT the diffuse-carrier seam; there is NO open GDN-scan seam (raw 0.0 vs native). The BV-match path does not need pursuing, and the spill workaround it would have required is moot for losslessness. The 22-flip diffuse carrier must live elsewhere (full-attn / deeper compounding / a non-scan sub-op), not in the GDN-scan launch geometry.

test.summary: THE QUESTION (is GDN-scan launch geometry BV=32/w4-vs-BV=16/w8 the diffuse-carrier seam?) is answered NO, decisively, on the first live GPU A/B. Captured bit-identical real cat9 layer-0 GDN scan inputs from a live verify forward (tree_n=10, n_pad=16, accepted_len=0, full tree with real branches) and ran our committed _tree_gdn_kernel at BV=16/w8 and BV=32/w4 plus the co-resident native fused_sigmoid_gating on the SAME inputs. RAW max_abs (the 0.0 gate, not atol): D16_npad1=0.0, D32_npad1=0.0, D16_npad16=0.0, D32_npad16=0.0 — ALL FOUR ZERO, including the negative control. I did NOT declare a verdict on the bare zeros: the playbook says D16==0.0 means possible mis-wired native ref, so I disconfirmed mis-wiring three ways — (a) native out is non-degenerate (distinct rows 0.85/0.66 apart, native[0]==serving[0]); (b) an independent pure-torch fp32 root-node scan matches BOTH native and our-kernel to 0.0078 (pure bf16 output rounding, same for both = proves native is real and runs identical fp32 math); (c) raw fp32 accumulator STATE is byte-identical across geometries (0.0), so bf16 store isn't hiding a sub-ULP diff. Extra geometry sweep (bv32w8, bv16w4, bv8w8) also all 0.0 vs bv16w8 and vs native. CONCLUSION: launch geometry does NOT change our kernel's fp32 reduction on GB10/triton 3.6.0 (the axis=1 reduction is over DIM_K within each V-row; BLOCK_V only re-tiles V-rows, not K-order), and our GDN scan is ALREADY byte-identical to native — there is NO open scan seam. The FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM_SCAN's "~1 bf16-ULP/node from reduction-tree reshape" was a CPU source-read prediction this GPU A/B refutes. Implication: the BV-match path and its spill-workaround are MOOT for losslessness; the diffuse 22-flip carrier is NOT the GDN-scan geometry and must be hunted elsewhere (full-attn depth / deeper-layer compounding / a non-scan sub-op). Host memory recovered, container torn down, GPU free. Artifacts (all absolute): /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_bv_ab/bv_ab_results.json (the verdict JSON), /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_bv_ab/bv_ab_replay.py (the 3-kernel replay), /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_bv_ab/diag2_geom.py + diag3_fp32out.py (the disconfirmation checks), /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_bv_ab/logs/fr13_bv_ab_capture.pt (the paired capture). The capture hook (default-OFF, env-gated FR13_BV_AB_CAPTURE) was added to scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py (~L4124, after launch_tree_gdn_prepared) with a 2-line default-empty passthrough in scripts/fr13_launch_forked_fa2_tree_server.sh — behavior-preserving for the locked path, banked alongside the other capture diagnostics; no kernel source edited.

The replay (bv_ab_replay.py run_kernel) reads the SAME cap[...] tensors for every geometry arm (BV16/w8 and BV32/w4), so all three arms share one input set — no cross-boot, no second forward, no input noise. Decisive cross-check: the live serving BV=16 output (serving_tree_out) == native to 0.0 at every path0 node, and the replay's own BV16 run == serving (d16_vs_serving_root/full = 0.0), so the replay kernel is wired to the same inputs as the live serve.
verify.nativeRefReal: CONFIRMED native is the real fused_sigmoid_gating kernel (BV=32/warps=4 internally), NOT our kernel again. The patch hook (L4171-4200) calls fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update directly, distinct from launch_tree_gdn_prepared. The negative-control's PURPOSE (D16 must be nonzero) is to catch a mis-wired ref; it came out 0.0, so I did NOT trust the bare zero — I ran the strongest independent disconfirmation: a from-scratch pure-torch fp32 rank-1 GDN scan of the root node matches native root to 0.007802 (=1 bf16 output ULP) AND matches our serving root to the SAME 0.007802, with native root == serving root = 0.0 exactly. That proves native is a genuine, correct, SEPARATE code path running identical fp32 math, not an alias of our kernel. native is also non-degenerate (rows differ 0.85/0.66, absmax 3.92, nonzero-frac 1.0). So D16=0.0 is a TRUE match, not a mis-wiring; the negative control did not 'fail to fire' — its premise (a seam exists) is simply false.

verify.bindsS1OrPerNodeOnly: Binds the NEGATIVE of S1 (per-node AND per-tree), not S1-as-carrier. The test DECISIVELY proves the GDN-scan launch geometry (BV/num_warps) is NOT a divergence source: our scan is ALREADY raw-0.0 byte-identical to native at every geometry (BV16/w8, BV32/w4, +swept bv32w8/bv16w4/bv8w8 all 0.0), so D32==0.0 is NOT 'geometry is the seam+fix' — it is 'there is no seam to fix'. This REFUTES the FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM_SCAN CPU prediction that the tl.sum(axis=1) reduction-tree reshape gives ~1 bf16-ULP/node (the axis=1 reduction is over DIM_K within each V-row; BLOCK_V only re-tiles which V-rows a program owns, not the K-reduction order — so geometry is invariant on GB10/triton 3.6.0). It does NOT positively locate the 22-flip carrier, and the e2e greedy-flip re-gate is NOT re-run here (correctly — this test's only job was the scan-geometry seam; the drift-localize doc already flagged this seam 'no depth-growth signature, unlikely to BE the 7x carrier alone'). So: per-tree match proven, carrier-elsewhere implied, e2e re-gate still owed by whatever the next hypothesis is.

verify.issues: (1) The replay (bv_ab_replay.py) does NOT re-invoke native — it loads cap['out_native'] captured once in the forward. So the replay's negative control rests ENTIRELY on the capture-time native call; the bare D16=0.0 in the replay JSON is by itself ambiguous. This is adequately closed by (a) the live serving==native 0.0 at all path0 nodes and (b) my independent fp32 torch ref matching native to 1 bf16 ULP — but the replay JSON alone would not refute mis-wiring. (2) Native runs only the 6-node path0 SPINE chain (no off-spine branch oracle), so this test confirms scan-geometry losslessness on the SPINE only; the branch nodes (4 of 10) are compared our-BV16 vs our-BV32 (0.0) but have no native counterpart here (native MTP has no branch rows) — branch losslessness vs the SpecInfer/STree path-rerun oracle is NOT tested by this. (3) N_PAD=1 replay synthesizes 1x1 zero masks and feeds only node 0, a constructed single-node case rather than a captured single-node forward — fine for the root op but it is a reconstruction, not a separately-captured N_PAD=1 forward. (4) This is a per-forward/per-layer-0 match; it does not by itself re-establish the e2e 22-flip count — that re-gate is still owed by the next candidate fix. None of these are material to the verdict: the scan-geometry seam is refuted raw-0.0 on the spine at both N_PAD with a genuine native ref.
